profile_policy: Restored older preference is a benchmark assumption, not a production database update.
run_policy: Read cases only, not archive. Freeze inputs and as_of. No search, notifications or DB writes. Store model, prompt version, inputs hash, raw assessment, extracted output, cost and human review separately for every run. Do not overwrite baselines.
rubric: Subscriber fit and meaningful overall judgment
Useful non-obvious insight: evidence-supported alternatives or timing advantages, with a practical recommendation
Reachable ski session and practical action
Proportionate uncertainty, access risks and explicit assumptions
Extraction preserves assessment verdict and caveats
scoring: Human review per dimension: 0 material failure, 1 partly useful, 2 good. Do not combine scores into an automatic storm verdict. Factual failures must be fixed even if the overall verdict matches.
limitations: Four historical cases plus one explicitly hypothetical paired follow-up; a development set, not a validation benchmark.
No forced one-case-per-verdict distribution; no user-confirmed Drop Everything case yet.
Operational claims lack captured source-page evidence.
Profile restoration and prompt changes must be tested separately to avoid attributing preference improvements to prompting.
Keep future unseen cases for validation rather than tuning on the whole archive.
design_principle: Evaluate quality of insight and evidence-supported judgment. Case notes are human discussion references, not answer keys or rules to feed to the model.
